mechanisms.name: Endpoint Security framework
mechanisms.note: an authorization client could veto exec system-wide, but it requires the com.apple.developer.endpoint-security.client entitlement, which Apple grants case by case, plus a system extension and full disk access. It is also a global authorizer, not a per-operation domain.

mechanisms.name: POSIX process group and session
mechanisms.note: the only grouping a plain macOS supervisor can create. A descendant leaves it with setsid, so it is not an unescapable domain.
mechanisms.observation: detached-descendant-membership=membership-renounced (expectation did not hold); detached-descendant-survives=survivor (expectation did not hold); attached-descendant-terminated=no-survivor (expectation held)

mechanisms.name: Supervisor deadline (context cancellation plus a process-group signal)
mechanisms.note: the only way to bound wall-clock time, because no resource limit expresses it. Cancelling a supervised process signals that process alone; the descendants it created need a separate group-directed signal, and a descendant that left the group needs its pid to have been recorded in advance.
mechanisms.observation: wall-clock:deadline-terminates-the-domain-root=no-survivor (expectation held); wall-clock:deadline-reaches-the-attached-descendant=survivor (expectation did not hold); wall-clock:deadline-reaches-the-detached-descendant=survivor (expectation did not hold); wall-clock:deadline-cancellation-leaves-no-descendant=1 survivors (expectation did not hold)

mechanisms.name: setrlimit RLIMIT_NOFILE
mechanisms.note: per process. A child inherits the same soft limit as a fresh budget, so a parent and a child together pass it. The soft limit can be lowered without the hard limit, in which case a domain member can raise it back; lowering the hard limit closes that route but is irreversible for the process that does it.
mechanisms.observation: descriptors:per-process-bound-binds=bound-binds (expectation held); descriptors:descendant-shares-the-declared-budget=per-process-only (expectation did not hold)

mechanisms.name: setrlimit RLIMIT_CPU
mechanisms.note: per process, in whole seconds, delivered as SIGXCPU at the soft limit and SIGKILL at the hard limit. Each descendant receives its own fresh CPU budget under the same declared bound.
mechanisms.observation: cpu-milliseconds:bound-can-be-declared=bound-installed (expectation held); cpu-milliseconds:bound-binds-the-process-that-set-it=refused-at-the-bound (expectation held); cpu-milliseconds:descendant-shares-the-declared-budget=per-process-only (expectation did not hold); cpu-milliseconds:member-cannot-raise-its-own-bound=member-restored-its-budget (expectation did not hold)

mechanisms.name: setrlimit RLIMIT_AS (RLIMIT_RSS on Darwin)
mechanisms.note: the interface exists and the resource number is defined, but this kernel refuses any soft limit below the address space the calling process has already reserved. A Go process reserves far more than a build budget, so no usable address-space bound can be installed from inside one.
mechanisms.observation: address-space-bytes:bound-can-be-declared=install-refused (expectation did not hold); address-space-bytes:some-bound-is-accepted-by-the-kernel=a-larger-bound-is-accepted (expectation held)

mechanisms.name: setrlimit RLIMIT_DATA
mechanisms.note: same refusal as RLIMIT_AS on this kernel, and it bounds the data segment rather than mapped memory, so it would not bound an mmap-based allocator even if it installed.
mechanisms.observation: data-segment-bytes:bound-can-be-declared=install-refused (expectation did not hold); data-segment-bytes:some-bound-is-accepted-by-the-kernel=a-larger-bound-is-accepted (expectation held)

mechanisms.name: setrlimit RLIMIT_NPROC
mechanisms.note: accounted per real user id, not per operation. The budget is shared with every other process the user already has, so a bound sized for a build domain refuses the domain's first process.
mechanisms.observation: process-count:bound-can-be-declared=bound-installed (expectation held); process-count:bound-binds-the-process-that-set-it=refused-at-the-bound (expectation held); process-count:declared-budget-is-available-to-the-domain=budget-consumed-outside-the-domain (expectation did not hold)

mechanisms.name: Filesystem quotas (edquota, quotacheck)
mechanisms.note: per user or group on a whole volume, requires root, and is not enabled on a default APFS install. It cannot bound the bytes one operation writes below one private directory.

mechanisms.name: Disk image (hdiutil) as a size-bounded private volume
mechanisms.note: a fixed-size attached image does bound bytes written below the build root, which is the one aggregate quantity macOS can enforce without private interfaces. It costs an attach and detach per operation and still does not bound memory, processes, CPU or time.
mechanisms.observation: not exercised by this run; the status above is a reading of the published interface, not a measurement

mechanisms.name: Virtualization.framework guest
mechanisms.note: a guest is an unescapable domain with aggregate memory and CPU bounds and atomic destruction. It is the only public macOS mechanism that satisfies the three blocking classes, at the cost of a guest image in the trusted computing base and a much larger per-operation setup.
mechanisms.observation: not exercised by this run; the status above is a reading of the published interface, not a measurement

mechanisms.name: chroot
mechanisms.note: requires root and is not a security boundary on macOS. It does not remove the global path namespace for a process that can create a new root, and it does not bound anything else.
